title: automated-orphaned-api-key-recovery-and-scope-aware-rotation
creator: Maya Singh
description: Problem: Over time we accumulate service and user API keys that have no active owner, are misnamed, or were created without per-scope TTLs. This increases blast radius for credential exposure and makes audit trails noisy. Goal: implement an automated orphaned API key discovery + recovery system and a scope-aware rotation policy that enforces metadata standards for provenance and expiration. The feature will (1) enrich audit logs with token provenance and scope tags, (2) enforce human-readable naming conventions and required metadata on creation, (3) introduce per-scope policy templates (e.g., service-infra, analytics-readonly, embedder) with default TTL/rotation cadence, and (4) run a reclaim workflow that notifies last-known owners, attempts automated rotation where possible, and quarantines keys that remain unclaimed.
acceptance_criteria: Discovery: Daily job identifies tokens with no activity >90 days, missing required provenance tags, or whose owner is inactive; results stored in admin audit index.
Metadata enforcement: Token creation API rejects keys missing required fields (owner_id OR owner_team, scope, environment) with clear error codes and migration guidance.
Per-scope policy engine: Admin UI and API allow creating/editing scope templates that define default TTL, rotation cadence, and allowed capabilities.
Reclamation workflow: Unclaimed tokens enter a 14-day notify -> 7-day automated rotation -> quarantine path; quarantine prevents further use and emits high-severity audit events.
Audit enrichment: Every token lifecycle event (create, rotate, revoke, quarantine, reclaim) emits structured audit logs with token_id, subject, scope, ticket ref, and migration link.
Rollout: Feature enabled behind flag and can be toggled per-customer for Private/Dedicated; default on for internal orgs.
Backwards compatibility: Existing tokens without metadata are discoverable and can be bulk-tagged via migration script; no automatic destruction without human approval.
Observability: Grafana dashboard shows daily orphaned-token count, reclamation success rate, and time-to-rotation metrics; alerts created for >1% per-week growth.
Security review: Design doc reviewed and approved by Security and Privacy teams with threat model and mitigation notes.
Docs & runbook: Public admin docs and an internal incident runbook for handling false-positive quarantines are published.
tasks: Design RBAC mappings to allow reclamation-worker only minimal privileges (token:list, token:rotate, token:tag)
Extend token schema: add required fields owner_id, owner_team, scope, created_via and validate in TokenService
Implement discovery worker (k8s CronJob) that flags candidate orphan tokens and writes to audit index
Build reclamation orchestration service: notify -> auto-rotate via owner-approved integrations -> quarantine if unclaimed
Add audit log schema fields and wire to central logging pipeline (structured JSON events)
Create Admin Console UI: Orphan list, per-token details, one-click claim/rotate/quarantine actions, and bulk tag workflow
Migration tooling: bulk-tagging script for historical tokens and a dry-run mode to preview changes
End-to-end tests including tenant isolation, Private-mode toggle, and failure modes where rotation fails
Monitoring: Grafana dashboard, Prometheus metrics, and PagerDuty alert for spike in orphaned tokens
Write docs: Admin guide, API reference changes, and internal runbook for false positives
notes: 2025-01-30: Initial design review with Security. Action: add quarantine audit event and retention policy (retention=7y for high-severity events). - Maya
2025-02-07: PM feedback (Ishita Rao): require a customer opt-out path for Dedicated/Private during migrations. Added toggle gating in rollout plan.
2025-02-18: Eng sync: decided to implement discovery as a separate idempotent worker to limit blast radius. Preference for incremental rollouts per-org.
2025-02-25: Prototype: discovery worker found ~1.4k candidate tokens in internal org; 42% lacked owner_team. Shared sample export in Slack (#sec-token-gov).

2025-03-01: Security review completed. Threat model notes: rotation of long-lived infra keys may break backfills; mitigation: rotation staging and auto-retry logic plus explicit owner approval endpoint.
2025-03-04: PR opened for token schema changes: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7243 (focus: validation and migration dry-run). Marked for 2 reviewer approvals.

Trade-offs discussed: aggressive auto-rotation reduces exposure but increases risk of service disruption. Solution: conservative default policy (notify -> owner-approve -> auto-rotate) with emergency override for critical compromises.
Edge cases: service accounts used by external partners where owner is unknown. Plan: create 'partner' scope with extended TTL and manual reclamation flow plus contract review.
Localization: Admin UI strings will need i18n; PM requested to defer to Localization team after MVP launch.
Runbook excerpt: If a production job fails post-rotation, use rollback endpoint to reissue previous key and escalate to the on-call infra team. Ensure runs are idempotent.
